questions.question: A developer needs realistic order records for unit tests. The records must not contain personal information. How should the developer use GitHub Copilot?

options.text: Reference the order schema and ask for synthetic records that use clearly fake names and example.com email addresses
options.why: Correct. Copilot can generate data in the required shape without exposing real personal data.

options.text: Paste a sample of production orders into the prompt so that Copilot can copy the format
options.why: Real customer data must not be placed in prompts.

options.text: Add the production database export to the repository and let Copilot read it as context
options.why: This exposes real personal data in the repository and in prompts.

options.text: Ask Copilot to retrieve records from the production database
options.why: Test data should be synthetic, and production data should not be used.

questions.explanation: Ask for fake data in a precise format and point Copilot at the schema, never at real records.

questions.question: A developer is assigned to modernize a legacy JavaScript module that has no documentation and no tests. What should the developer do first?

options.text: Use /explain to understand the module and then add tests that capture its current behavior
options.why: Correct. Understanding and pinning the current behavior make it possible to verify the modernized code.

options.text: Ask Copilot agent mode to rewrite the entire module in a single change
options.why: A large rewrite without tests is difficult to review and verify.

options.text: Delete the module and ask Copilot to generate a new one from its file name
options.why: Copilot cannot reproduce behavior it has not seen, and callers may break.

options.text: Enable content exclusion for the module
options.why: Excluding the module prevents Copilot from using it as context.

questions.explanation: Explain first, then write characterization tests, then modernize in small, reviewed steps.

questions.question: A team uses GitHub Copilot to convert a callback-based Node.js module to async/await. Which TWO practices reduce the risk of introducing defects?

options.text: Convert one function or file at a time and review each diff
options.why: Correct. Small changes are easier to review and isolate when a test fails.

options.text: Run the existing and characterization tests after each change
options.why: Correct. Tests confirm that each step keeps the same behavior.

options.text: Accept the full module rewrite because Copilot executed the code during generation
options.why: Copilot does not execute code to validate suggestions.

options.text: Disable the tests during the conversion to avoid failures
options.why: Disabling tests removes the check that detects behavior changes.

questions.explanation: Modernize incrementally and verify each step with tests.

questions.question: A developer uses GitHub Copilot to translate business logic from an older, rarely used programming language to C#. The translated code compiles. What should the developer consider before deploying it?

options.text: Suggestions can be less reliable for less common languages, so the code must be tested against known outputs from the original system
options.why: Correct. Details such as rounding and data types can change during translation.

options.text: Code that compiles is guaranteed to have the same behavior as the original
options.why: Compiling does not confirm that the logic is equivalent.

options.text: Copilot validates translated code against the original program before returning it
options.why: Copilot does not run either program.

options.text: Translation is safe only when the public code filter is set to Block
options.why: The public code filter does not verify functional equivalence.

questions.explanation: Copilot can help translate code, but output for rare languages needs careful testing.

questions.question: A developer wants GitHub Copilot to modernize a legacy report module, update the two files that call it, and run the test suite, with the developer approving terminal commands. Which Copilot Chat mode should the developer use?

options.text: Agent mode
options.why: Correct. Agent mode determines which files to change, edits them and runs commands such as tests after approval.

options.text: Ask mode
options.why: Ask mode answers questions and suggests code but does not edit files or run commands.

options.text: Edit mode with no files selected
options.why: Edit mode applies changes to files the developer chooses and does not run terminal commands.

options.text: Inline suggestions only
options.why: Inline suggestions complete code at the cursor and do not run tests.

questions.explanation: Agent mode can plan multi-file changes, run tests after approval and iterate on failures.
